headings.title: SMTO-GML-0054 — This Gmail action needs an account that signs in through Google

html:
SMTO-GML-0054 — This Gmail action needs an account that signs in through Google

GUID: 7ee99a77-39ed-5373-aa4a-b37e137f87b1
Slug: gmail-oauth-operation-required
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gmail_imap

What happened

  • Your Gmail account is connected with an app password. That lets SMTO read, send and organize mail, but not manage filters, label colors or visibility, or Gmail's built-in folders as labels. SMTO didn't make this change.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. To move mail in or out of Inbox or Trash, ask SMTO to archive, move to Trash, restore from Trash, mark read or unread, or star the messages instead. These actions work with an app-password account, while adding or removing Gmail's built-in folders as labels does not.
  2. For filters, label colors, or hiding labels, make the change yourself in Gmail on the web under Settings › See all settings. Gmail only allows these settings through its website or a Google sign-in, not through an app password.
  3. If you want SMTO to do these changes, ask the person who manages SMTO to add a Gmail account that signs in through Google, then mention that account with @ in a new request. SMTO never changes which account a request uses on its own, so you choose the account deliberately.

What success looks like

  • The request finishes with a supported action, or the change appears in Gmail after you make it there.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete or replace your app-password account to get past this; it is still needed for everyday mail tasks.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The requested method is outside the app-password IMAP/SMTP adapter: filters, label visibility or color, adding or removing system labels (TRASH, SPAM, DRAFT, SENT, ALL) as labels, or an unrecognized method.

What this means

  • The requested operation is outside the Gmail IMAP and SMTP adapter contract. Confirmed substeps and effect_unknown remain authoritative. This diagnostic alone does not establish whether a prior write or send completed.

Why this can happen

  • Producer condition: The requested operation is outside the Gmail IMAP and SMTP adapter contract.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the exact account revision, Gateway route and failing substep with the retained receipt.

How to fix it

  • Use a supported app-password method (for example trash_message, archive by removing INBOX, read/star flags, custom labels) or rerun the operation with an explicitly selected OAuth account (gmail_account or google_account with the needed scopes). Filter methods map to gmail_oauth_required, system-label modify to gmail_imap_label_operation_unsupported and unknown methods to gmail_imap_operation_unsupported; the agent never switches account_ref automatically.
  • Choose an explicitly configured Gmail OAuth account for this operation, or use one of the supported app-password mailbox actions. The agent will not switch accounts automatically.

Retry and execution caution

  • Preserve confirmed work and establish the current mailbox state before any repeated write.

How to verify the fix

  • The chosen operation completes with a matching receipt, or the remaining uncertain action is inspected in Gmail without duplicate mail.

What not to do

  • Do not switch accounts or authentication methods after failure, or automatically replay uncertain writes.

Technical notes

  • Confirmed substeps and effect_unknown remain authoritative. This diagnostic alone does not establish whether a prior write or send completed.
  • App-password setup: https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/185833
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
